title: Key to Common Families of Adult Odonata

couplets.text: Forewing and hindwing differ in size and shape, with hindwing much broader basally than forewing [suborder Anisoptera]
Forewing and hindwing similar in size and shape
Triangles in forewing and hindwing similar in shape and pointing the same direction; hindwing without a foot-shaped anal loop
Triangles in forewing and hindwing differ in shape and pointing in different directions; hindwing with a foot-shaped anal loop

title: Key to Common Families of Orthoptera

couplets.text: Antennae relatively short (shorter than body); ovipositor small; tympana on first abdominal segment [suborder Caelifera]
Antennae longer than body; ovipositor usually long and conspicuous; tympana (when present) on fore tibiae [suborder Ensifera]
Tarsi with 3 tarsomeres
Tarsi with 4 tarsomeres
Tympana present on foretibiae
Fore tibiae without tympana

title: Key to Common Families of Hemiptera

couplets.text: Mouthparts originate below or behind the eyes; scutellum usually reduced and indistinct; forewings not hemelytra, held rooflike over abdomen
Mouthparts originate in front of eyes; scutellum large and distinct; forewings in the form of hemelytra, held flat over abdomen [suborder Heteroptera]
Antennae long, threadlike [suborder Sternorrhyncha]
Antennae short, bristlelike (setaceous or aristate) [suborder Auchenorrhyncha]
Cornicles present near the posterior end of abdomen; wingless or with 2 pairs of wings; 3 pairs of legs always present
Cornicles absent; wingless or with 1 pair of wings; females often legless
Aristate antennae with a bulbous pedicel; antennae originate below the eyes
Antennae usually setaceous, pedicel not particularly enlarged; antennae originate in front of or between the eyes
Relatively large insects (usually 3 cm or more in length); 3 prominent ocelli
Usually much smaller insects; 2 ocelli (not always obvious)
Pronotum greatly expanded and extending over the abdomen
Pronotum not expanded
Hind tibiae with 1 or 2 stout spines and an apical ring of spines
Hind tibiae with 1 or more rows of smaller spines
Antennae very short; aquatic species
Antennae longer than head; aquatic or terrestrial species
Large, raptorial forelegs; relatively long, thin beak
Forelegs reduced, tarsi scoop-shaped; beak small, short, broad, and rounded
Aquatic bugs that live on the water surface; middle and hind legs very long and slender
Terrestrial bugs; middle and hind legs usually not so long and slender
Scutellum very large, extending to the end of abdomen
Scutellum smaller, not reaching end of abdomen
Body flat and oval-shaped; wings vestigial and non-functional
Wings not vestigial
Antennae 5-segmented; body shield-shaped; scutellum large
Antennae 4-segmented; body usually more elongate; scutellum smaller
Beak 3-segmented; wing venation simple
Beak 4-segmented; wing venation simple or complex
Membrane of hemelytra with many veins
Membrane of hemelytra with no more than 5 veins
Cuneus present; membrane of hemelytra with 1 or 2 closed cells
Cuneus absent; membrane of hemelytra with 4 or 5 veins
